key_insight: Medical image encoders only show modest convergence, and that similarity is driven more by self-supervised pretraining than by clinical supervision or model scale.
clinical_relevance: A classifier learned on one encoder can transfer to others and to external hospitals, but the shared representation is still imperfect and may not match how clinicians judge similarity.
method: Compared 18 image and 7 text encoders across five imaging modalities and 650,982 chest radiographs.
Controlled training so only the objective changed, keeping data, architecture, and scale fixed.
Tested representation alignment, scaling effects, and transfer performance against clinical judgment.
evidence_signal: Across chest radiography, matched self-supervised encoders aligned most (40.4%), while label-supervised (21.1%) and image-text models (3.3%) aligned less, with no clear increase from model size.
watch_item: The shared geometry is limited within modalities and may be weakest across patient subgroups, so interoperability should be validated before clinical deployment.
paper_title: Self-supervision drives representational convergence in medical foundation models more than clinical supervision
